features_mcp_sec_1: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE: you approve each assistant on an OpenAthlete page. It never sees your password.
features_mcp_sec_2: Read and write are separate. An assistant with read access is not even offered the tools that write.
features_mcp_sec_3: Tokens are stored hashed. Access tokens last an hour; refresh tokens are single-use, and a stolen one used twice revokes the access.
features_mcp_sec_4: Personal tokens last 30, 90 or 365 days, or never expire. Revoke any connection in Settings › AI agents; it stops at the next request.
features_mcp_sec_5: Assistants reach your training, not your account: no password change, no device or subscription change, no deleting your history.
features_mcp_sec_note: What an assistant does with your data is up to it and its provider. Connect the ones you trust.
features_mcp_faq_1_a: Yes, on every plan, Free included, and on self-hosted instances. The model runs on your assistant's side, under your Claude or ChatGPT account.
features_mcp_faq_2_a: Claude (claude.ai, desktop, mobile and Claude Code), ChatGPT in developer mode, Cursor, VS Code and any MCP client that supports OAuth or a bearer token.
features_mcp_faq_3_q: Can the assistant delete my activities?

features_sync_strava_a: Yes, as soon as Strava has it, with full streams
features_sync_strava_o: No: Strava has no planned workouts
features_sync_garmin_a: Yes, pushed by Garmin, with the FIT file and laps
features_sync_garmin_h: The last 30 days, imported when you connect
features_sync_garmin_w: Sleep stages and score, HRV, resting HR, stress, Body Battery, SpO2, body composition, VO2max, blood pressure
features_sync_garmin_o: Yes: to the Garmin Connect calendar and the watch
features_sync_polar_a: Yes, by notification plus an hourly safety check
features_sync_polar_h: None: only activities recorded after you connect
features_sync_polar_w: Daily activity, sleep, nightly HRV, weight, VO2max, max and resting HR
features_sync_polar_o: No: Polar's API does not accept planned workouts
features_sync_suunto_h: The last 30 days, imported when you connect
features_sync_suunto_w: Sleep stages and score, HRV, daily HR, steps, calories, SpO2, naps, resources
features_sync_coros_a: Yes, checked about every 30 minutes (COROS has no push)
features_sync_coros_h: Full history, slowly: COROS serves 50 files a day, so years of runs take several days
features_sync_coros_w: HRV, resting HR, sleep, naps, VO2max
features_sync_files_a: Yes: upload several at once or drop one on a calendar day. FIT and TCX keep laps
features_sync_api_a: Yes: other apps push FIT, GPX or TCX files over OAuth 2.1
features_sync_ical_o: Planned sessions, races and notes to Google, Apple or Outlook Calendar
features_sync_brand_garmin: Activities, the last 30 days, wellness, and workouts to the watch.
features_sync_brand_coros: The newest connector. Full history, workouts for run, trail and bike.
features_sync_brand_suunto: Activities, wellness, and workouts as Suunto guides.
features_sync_brand_polar: New activities and wellness in. No workouts out.
features_sync_brand_strava: Activities and full history. Nothing goes back.
features_sync_pipe_title: What happens to every new activity
features_sync_pipe_body: Whatever the source, each activity goes through the same steps a few seconds after it lands. That is why a Polar run and a COROS run end up comparable.
features_sync_pipe_7: AI questions and read, if enabled
features_sync_team_body: One athlete on a Forerunner, one on a COROS Pace, one on a Polar Vantage, one who only uses Strava. You see all of them on the same dashboard, plan them the same way, and each structured session goes to whichever watch can take it. Nobody has to change brand to work with you.
features_sync_neutral_body: On 22 July 2026, Garmin bought TrainingPeaks. Nothing announced says TrainingPeaks will treat other watches differently. But your training platform now belongs to a watch maker, and that is a fair thing to think about. OpenAthlete belongs to no brand, its code is public, and your data leaves in one JSON export whenever you want.
features_sync_self_body: Strava, Garmin, Polar and Suunto each require a developer or partner account with the brand, so most self-hosted servers start with COROS (no vendor account needed), file upload and the Activity Import API.
features_sync_faq_1_q: Can I connect several services at once?
features_sync_faq_1_a: Yes, for example Garmin for workouts and wellness, and Strava to bring in your older history. If two services send you the same activities, turn off activity import on one of them in its sync options.
features_sync_faq_2_q: Do Polar watches receive planned workouts?
features_sync_faq_2_a: No. Polar's API does not accept them. Polar activities and wellness data come in normally. Workouts go to Garmin, Suunto and COROS.
features_sync_faq_3_q: What about Wahoo, Zwift or Apple Health?
features_sync_faq_3_a: Not connected yet. Most of them can export FIT files, which you can upload, or send activities to Strava, which syncs with OpenAthlete.
features_sync_faq_4_q: How far back does the history go?
features_sync_faq_4_a: It depends on the brand. Strava and COROS bring your full history (COROS at 50 files a day, so it takes a few days). Garmin and Suunto import the last 30 days when you connect. Polar only sends activities recorded after you connect. Older files can always be uploaded as FIT, GPX or TCX.
features_sync_faq_5_q: What happens when I disconnect a service or delete my account?
features_sync_faq_5_a: Deleting your account erases everything you own and deregisters OpenAthlete from Garmin, Polar, Suunto and the others. Before that, you can download all your data as one JSON file.
features_sync_faq_6_q: Is sync part of a paid plan?
features_sync_faq_6_a: No. Every connection, history import and workout export is free. Supporter only adds AI on our keys and unlimited coached athletes.
features_sync_final_title: Connect your watch in a minute
features_sync_final_body: Create an account, pick your brand, and watch your activities fill the calendar.
mobile_seo_title: OpenAthlete app for iPhone and Android
mobile_seo_description: Your training calendar, workouts and form in your pocket. Install the OpenAthlete web app on iPhone or Android today; native apps are in testing.
mobile_lead: The OpenAthlete web app already works on your phone: today's session, the week ahead, your activities, messages with your coach. Put it on your home screen in three taps. The native iPhone and Android apps are in testing.
mobile_shot_alt_home: Today screen of the OpenAthlete app on a phone
mobile_shot_alt_chat: Messages with a coach on a phone
mobile_status_web_body: Any recent phone browser. Install it from Safari or Chrome.
mobile_status_ios_body: In testing on TestFlight. No release date yet.
mobile_status_android_body: In testing on Google Play. No release date yet.
mobile_watch_title: Want to know when they ship?
mobile_watch_body: Every release is published on GitHub. Click Watch, then Custom › Releases, and GitHub tells you when a new version lands. No mailing list, no email to give us.
mobile_today_title: Built for the phone, not shrunk onto it
mobile_today_lead: Under 768 pixels wide, OpenAthlete switches to a phone layout: tabs at the bottom, screens that stack, sheets that slide up.
mobile_f1_body: The first tab: today's session or rest day, your form, this week done against planned, days left to your next race.
mobile_f2_body: Days stack vertically with their sessions, totals and the zone profile of each workout.
mobile_f3_title: Log RPE and how you feel
mobile_f3_body: Rate the effort, add a comment for your coach, answer the questions after each activity.
mobile_f4_body: One-to-one and group conversations, in real time, with notices when a new activity comes in.
mobile_install_title: On your home screen in three taps
mobile_install_lead: It opens full screen, without the browser bar, like any other app. The app also shows these steps the first time you open it on a phone.
mobile_ios_1: Open app.openathlete.org in Safari and sign in.
mobile_ios_2: Tap the Share button, the square with an arrow pointing up.
mobile_android_1: Open app.openathlete.org in Chrome and sign in.
mobile_android_2: Tap the ⋮ menu at the top right.
mobile_android_3: Choose "Install app" (or "Add to Home screen"), then confirm.
mobile_native_1: A notification when your activity is processed, with the questions ready to answer.
mobile_native_2: A reminder at 7 pm the day before a planned session, in your time zone. You can turn it off.
mobile_native_3: Sign in with Apple or Google, and voice answers recorded in the app.
mobile_native_4: A custom server address, for people who self-host OpenAthlete.
mobile_watchapp_body: Garmin Connect, COROS, Suunto or Polar Flow still sync your watch. OpenAthlete picks the activities up from there and sends planned workouts back to Garmin, Suunto and COROS.
mobile_offline_body: There is no offline mode yet. Without a connection, the app asks you to reconnect. Your watch keeps recording, of course.
mobile_faq_1_q: When will the iPhone and Android apps be available?
mobile_faq_1_a: They are in testing on TestFlight and Google Play. We will not give a date we cannot promise. Watch the releases on GitHub to be told when they ship.
mobile_faq_2_q: Is the web app the full product?
mobile_faq_2_a: Yes. It is the same app as on a computer, with a phone layout: calendar, workouts, activities, statistics, coaching and messages.
mobile_faq_3_a: No. Like the rest of OpenAthlete, they are free. Supporter stays optional and only adds AI on our keys and unlimited coached athletes.
mobile_faq_4_q: Does the web app send notifications?
mobile_faq_4_a: Not today. Push notifications come with the native apps. Unread messages are still sent to you by email.
mobile_faq_5_q: I self-host OpenAthlete. Can I use it on my phone?
mobile_faq_5_a: Yes. Install your instance's web app the same way, from its own address. The native apps will let you enter a custom server address.
mobile_final_title: Start on the web, keep it in your pocket
mobile_final_body: Create a free account, connect your watch, then add OpenAthlete to your home screen.

features_hub_loop_1_body: Season, blocks, races, week by week.

features_hub_cal_p2: Illness, injury and travel periods that move sessions
features_hub_cal_p3: A private feed for Google, Apple or Outlook Calendar

features_hub_an_5_body: 400 m to 100 km, power by duration, best of each year. Exclude a GPS glitch in one click.
features_hub_an_6_body: Critical speed, critical power and critical swim speed from what you actually did, with race-time ranges.
features_hub_an_7_body: Pace or power against heart rate, first half against second.
features_hub_an_8_body: Volume, intensity distribution, durability, recovery trends. Compare periods, export CSV.
